newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita says may lose FIM 300 mln in EMU [CORRECTED 09:35 GMT].
newsitem.headline: Merita says may lose FIM 300 mln in EMU [CORRECTED 09:35 GMT].

text.p: Finnish banking group Merita Oy said on Thursday it expected to lose no more than 200 million to 300 million markka in revenue if Finland joins the third stage of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
This annual shortfall would come on top of earlier estimated direct transition costs of 200 million markka.

"According to current estimates, the net impact appears negative. However, the maximum annual loss of income is unlikely to exceed 200 to 300 million markka," Merita said in its January-September interim report.
The third phase of EMU is due to begin in 1999.

Merita spokeswoman Eira Palin-Lehtinen said about 100 million markka of these losses would be in currency trading, about 100 million in other treasury operations and the rest would be lost in other monetary transactions.
In January-September this year, Merita's net income from securities trading totalled 873 million markka and its net income from foreign exchange dealing was 149 million markka.
In full-year 1995, excluding Kansallis-Osake-Pankki's KOPF.HE first quarter, Merita earned 773 million markka from trading securities and 270 million from trading currencies.
Merita group's other net commission income was 1.68 billion markka in January-September this year and 2.06 billion in full-year 1995.
